checklist.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity: Does get_beacon_proposer_index correctly return the pre-computed proposer from state.proposer_lookahead instead of performing on-demand computation?
checklist.test_procedure: 1. Locate all client implementations of get_beacon_proposer_index in consensus clients (Prysm, Lighthouse, Teku, Lodestar, Nimbus, Grandine). 2. Verify that the function body is exactly: return state.proposer_lookahead[state.slot % SLOTS_PER_EPOCH]. 3. Confirm no fallback to the legacy compute_proposer_index path exists in production code. 4. Construct a scenario where the beacon state has changed since the epoch boundary (e.g., a slashing reduces effective balance mid-epoch). 5. Verify that get_beacon_proposer_index still returns the pre-computed value from the lookahead array, NOT a recomputed value based on the current state. 6. Check that no conditional logic bypasses the lookahead (e.g., if proposer_lookahead is empty, fall back to on-demand computation). 7. Verify the boundary edge tb-009 (CL-to-Validator interface) correctly propagates the pre-computed proposer index to validator duty assignments.
executable_checks: Unit test: Mutate validator effective balances after epoch transition, verify get_beacon_proposer_index returns same proposer as pre-computed lookahead
Differential test: Compare get_beacon_proposer_index output against legacy compute_proposer_index for same state to detect any divergence scenario
Cross-client test: Run identical state through all CL clients and verify identical proposer_index output from get_beacon_proposer_index
checklist.notes: Source: PROP-0036, Invariant: FULU-SG005-INV-001, Trust Boundary: tb-009. EIP-7917 fundamentally changes proposer selection from on-demand to pre-computed. Any client that retains a fallback to the old computation would produce divergent results, causing a consensus split. This is particularly dangerous during the fork transition where the proposer_lookahead field is first populated.

checklist.title: Is the slot-to-lookahead-index mapping via state.slot % SLOTS_PER_EPOCH always within bounds [0, SLOTS_PER_EPOCH)?
checklist.test_procedure: 1. Identify all implementations of get_beacon_proposer_index across CL clients. 2. Verify the index computation uses state.slot % SLOTS_PER_EPOCH (not state.slot % len(proposer_lookahead) or any other formula). 3. Test boundary values: slot = 0, slot = SLOTS_PER_EPOCH - 1, slot = SLOTS_PER_EPOCH (first slot of next epoch), slot = MAX_SLOT. 4. Verify that the modulo result always produces an index in [0, 31] (for SLOTS_PER_EPOCH=32). 5. Check for any off-by-one errors where the implementation might use (state.slot - 1) % SLOTS_PER_EPOCH or (state.slot + 1) % SLOTS_PER_EPOCH. 6. Verify that the index correctly maps to the CURRENT epoch's proposer, not the next or previous epoch's proposer. 7. Test at epoch boundaries: confirm that the last slot of epoch N and the first slot of epoch N+1 map to different proposers from the lookahead array.
executable_checks: Property-based test: forall slot in [0, MAX_SLOT], (slot % SLOTS_PER_EPOCH) is in [0, SLOTS_PER_EPOCH)
Boundary test: Verify correct proposer at slot 0, slot 31, slot 32, slot 63 for epoch transitions
Fuzz test: Random slot values to verify no out-of-bounds access on proposer_lookahead array
checklist.notes: Source: PROP-0037, Invariant: FULU-SG005-INV-002. The modulo operation is mathematically guaranteed to produce values in [0, SLOTS_PER_EPOCH), but implementation bugs could arise from using the wrong divisor, signed integer division, or off-by-one adjustments. Note: bug_bounty_eligible=false but still in-scope for audit.

checklist.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity: Does get_beacon_proposer_indices use only active validators obtained via get_active_validator_indices(state, epoch)?
checklist.test_procedure: 1. Locate the implementation of get_beacon_proposer_indices in each CL client. 2. Verify the first step obtains indices via get_active_validator_indices(state, epoch) -- not from all validators, not from a cached set, and not from a different epoch. 3. Verify the epoch parameter passed to get_active_validator_indices matches the epoch for which proposers are being computed (especially N + MIN_SEED_LOOKAHEAD + 1 in process_proposer_lookahead). 4. Construct a state where a validator is active in epoch N but exits before epoch N + MIN_SEED_LOOKAHEAD + 1. 5. Verify the exiting validator is NOT included in the proposer selection pool for the future epoch. 6. Construct a state where a validator activates between the current epoch and the lookahead epoch. 7. Verify the newly active validator IS included in the selection pool for the correct epoch. 8. Check that no client uses a stale or memoized active validator set that might not reflect pending exits/activations for the target epoch.
executable_checks: Unit test: Create state with mix of active, exiting, and pending validators; verify only active ones are in proposer selection pool
Property-based test: forall epochs, proposer_indices subset_of active_validator_indices(epoch)
Regression test: State with validator exiting at epoch N+1 must not appear in proposer selection for epoch N+2
checklist.notes: Source: PROP-0038, Invariant: FULU-SG006-INV-001, Trust Boundary: tb-009. Including inactive validators in proposer selection would cause missed slots when those validators are selected, degrading network liveness. This is especially critical at the CL-Validator boundary where proposer duties are assigned.

checklist.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity: Is the proposer selection seed domain-separated using DOMAIN_BEACON_PROPOSER via get_seed(state, epoch, DOMAIN_BEACON_PROPOSER)?
checklist.test_procedure: 1. Locate the seed computation in get_beacon_proposer_indices across all CL clients. 2. Verify the seed is computed as get_seed(state, epoch, DOMAIN_BEACON_PROPOSER). 3. Confirm the domain type constant is DOMAIN_BEACON_PROPOSER and not any other domain (DOMAIN_BEACON_ATTESTER, DOMAIN_SYNC_COMMITTEE, etc.). 4. Verify that the domain separation constant value matches the spec exactly across all clients. 5. Construct a test where the same state and epoch produce DIFFERENT seeds when using DOMAIN_BEACON_PROPOSER vs. DOMAIN_BEACON_ATTESTER. 6. Verify that proposer selection with the correct domain produces a different ordering than attestation committee selection, confirming independence. 7. Check that no client accidentally hardcodes a domain value or uses a configuration-dependent value.
executable_checks: Unit test: Verify get_seed with DOMAIN_BEACON_PROPOSER produces different output than with any other domain constant
Cross-client test: All clients produce identical seed for same (state, epoch, DOMAIN_BEACON_PROPOSER) tuple
Static analysis: Grep all client codebases for get_seed or seed computation calls in proposer selection to verify correct domain usage
checklist.notes: Source: PROP-0039, Invariant: FULU-SG006-INV-002, Threat: stride-017, Trust Boundary: tb-009. Incorrect domain separation would correlate proposer selection with other randomness-dependent operations, potentially enabling MEV extraction through predictable proposer schedules. Note: bug_bounty_eligible=false but still in-scope for audit.

checklist.title: Can the epoch sub-process ordering in process_epoch be violated, causing process_proposer_lookahead to execute before all 15 preceding steps complete?
checklist.test_procedure: 1. Locate process_epoch in each CL client implementation. 2. Verify the exact order of all 16 sub-process calls matches the spec: (1) process_justification_and_finalization, (2) process_inactivity_updates, (3) process_rewards_and_penalties, (4) process_registry_updates, (5) process_slashings, (6) process_eth1_data_reset, (7) process_pending_deposits, (8) process_pending_consolidations, (9) process_effective_balance_updates, (10) process_slashings_reset, (11) process_randao_mixes_reset, (12) process_historical_summaries_update, (13) process_participation_flag_updates, (14) process_sync_committee_updates, (15) RESERVED/other, (16) process_proposer_lookahead. 3. Verify process_proposer_lookahead is the LAST step. 4. Check for any parallelization, async execution, or deferred computation that might cause steps to execute out of order. 5. Verify each sub-process operates on the mutated state from the previous step (not a snapshot or copy). 6. Construct a state where reordering steps 4 (registry_updates) and 16 (proposer_lookahead) produces different proposer assignments. 7. Verify that the correct ordering produces the expected proposer assignments while the incorrect ordering produces different (wrong) ones.
executable_checks: Static analysis: Parse process_epoch implementation in each client to extract call ordering; diff against spec
Differential test: Execute process_epoch with correct order vs. swapped order of last two steps; compare resulting beacon state roots
PoC: Construct a state with pending validator activation/exit where reordering process_registry_updates and process_proposer_lookahead produces different proposer lookahead arrays
checklist.notes: Source: PROP-0040, Invariant: FULU-SG007-INV-001, Assumption: asm-014. This is CRITICAL because executing epoch sub-processes out of order would produce different beacon states across clients, causing a consensus split. The proposer lookahead especially depends on finalized validator registry updates from step 4 (process_registry_updates) and effective balance updates from step 9. A formal verification paper (Nature, 2025) specifically addresses safety properties of epoch processing ordering.

checklist.title: Can process_proposer_lookahead be executed before preceding epoch sub-processes, causing it to use stale validator data for proposer computation?
checklist.test_procedure: 1. Verify process_proposer_lookahead is called after ALL of: process_registry_updates, process_effective_balance_updates, process_randao_mixes_reset, and process_slashings in every CL client. 2. Identify all state fields that process_proposer_lookahead depends on: (a) validator registry (active validators), (b) effective balances (proposer selection weighting), (c) randao_mixes (seed computation). 3. Trace the data flow: confirm each dependency is updated by a preceding sub-process. 4. Construct a test case: State has a validator with pending activation at the epoch boundary. Execute process_proposer_lookahead BEFORE process_registry_updates. 5. Verify the result incorrectly excludes the newly activated validator from the proposer pool. 6. Then execute in correct order and verify the newly activated validator IS included. 7. Compare the two resulting proposer_lookahead arrays -- they MUST differ, proving the ordering dependency. 8. Check for any client optimization that caches the active validator set before epoch processing begins and reuses it in process_proposer_lookahead.
executable_checks: PoC: State with validator activation_epoch == current_epoch + 1, show process_proposer_lookahead produces different results when run before vs. after process_registry_updates
PoC: State with validator being slashed, show proposer_lookahead differs when run before vs. after process_slashings + process_effective_balance_updates
Cross-client differential: Feed identical pre-epoch state to all clients, verify identical post-epoch proposer_lookahead arrays
checklist.notes: Source: PROP-0041, Invariant: FULU-SG007-INV-002, Assumption: asm-014. Computing the proposer lookahead before validator exits/activations are processed would include validators who should be inactive or exclude newly activated validators, causing incorrect proposer assignments across the network. This is a critical consensus split risk. The dependency on randao_mixes is especially subtle: process_randao_mixes_reset copies the current mix to the next epoch position, and the seed for proposer selection references this.

checklist.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity: Does the shift operation in process_proposer_lookahead remove exactly SLOTS_PER_EPOCH entries from the front of the lookahead array?
checklist.test_procedure: 1. Locate the shift operation in process_proposer_lookahead across all CL clients. 2. Verify the operation computes last_epoch_start = len(state.proposer_lookahead) - SLOTS_PER_EPOCH. 3. Verify the shift is: state.proposer_lookahead[:last_epoch_start] = state.proposer_lookahead[SLOTS_PER_EPOCH:]. 4. Test with a known proposer_lookahead array. Verify exactly the first SLOTS_PER_EPOCH entries are removed and all remaining entries shift left. 5. Test off-by-one: Change shift amount to SLOTS_PER_EPOCH - 1 and verify one stale entry remains at front. 6. Test off-by-one: Change shift amount to SLOTS_PER_EPOCH + 1 and verify one valid entry is lost. 7. Verify no entries in positions [SLOTS_PER_EPOCH, last_epoch_start) are modified or lost during the shift. 8. Check for language-specific array copy semantics that might cause aliasing issues (e.g., in Go, Rust, Java implementations). 9. Verify the shift preserves the correct relationship: after shift, proposer_lookahead[0] is the proposer for the first slot of the next epoch.
executable_checks: Unit test: Known lookahead [A0..A31, B0..B31], after shift first 32 entries should be [B0..B31]
Property-based test: forall lookahead arrays, after shift, len(shifted) == len(original) - SLOTS_PER_EPOCH (before fill)
Off-by-one test: Verify proposer_lookahead[0] after shift equals proposer_lookahead[SLOTS_PER_EPOCH] before shift
Aliasing test: Verify overlapping memory copy in Go/Rust implementations handles the copy correctly
checklist.notes: Source: PROP-0042, Invariant: FULU-SG008-INV-001, Assumption: asm-012, Threat: stride-011, Trust Boundary: tb-009. Shifting by the wrong amount would cause stale or missing proposer entries. In Go, copy() with overlapping slices is implementation-defined in some edge cases. In Rust, Vec drain/splice semantics must be verified. This directly affects the CL-Validator boundary (tb-009) because incorrect proposer assignments propagate to validator duty assignments.

checklist.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity: Are new proposer indices computed for the correct future epoch (N + MIN_SEED_LOOKAHEAD + 1) and appended to the correct positions in the lookahead array?
checklist.test_procedure: 1. Locate the fill operation in process_proposer_lookahead across all CL clients. 2. Verify the epoch for new proposer computation is: Epoch(get_current_epoch(state) + MIN_SEED_LOOKAHEAD + 1). 3. Check for off-by-one: Verify it is NOT get_current_epoch(state) + MIN_SEED_LOOKAHEAD (off by one). 4. Verify it is NOT get_current_epoch(state) + MIN_SEED_LOOKAHEAD + 2 (off by one in other direction). 5. Verify the new indices are written to positions [last_epoch_start:] of the lookahead array. 6. Verify exactly SLOTS_PER_EPOCH new entries are appended. 7. Construct a test: At epoch boundary N, verify the new entries correspond to proposers for epoch N + MIN_SEED_LOOKAHEAD + 1 by independently computing them. 8. Verify the epoch used for get_active_validator_indices matches the epoch used for get_seed in the proposer computation. 9. Check that get_current_epoch(state) returns the CORRECT epoch after the epoch transition has incremented the slot.
executable_checks: Unit test: At epoch N boundary, verify new entries match independently computed proposers for epoch N + MIN_SEED_LOOKAHEAD + 1
Off-by-one test: Compare proposers computed for epoch N+MSL+1 vs N+MSL vs N+MSL+2; all must differ
Cross-client test: All clients produce identical proposer_lookahead after epoch transition for the same pre-state
PoC: Show that using epoch N+MSL instead of N+MSL+1 produces wrong proposer assignments MSL+1 epochs later
checklist.notes: Source: PROP-0043, Invariant: FULU-SG008-INV-002, Trust Boundary: tb-009. An off-by-one in the epoch computation for new proposer indices is a subtle but critical bug. It would not manifest immediately -- only MIN_SEED_LOOKAHEAD + 1 epochs later when the incorrectly computed entries are consumed. This delayed manifestation makes it harder to detect in testing.

checklist.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity: Does the proposer_lookahead array maintain exactly (MIN_SEED_LOOKAHEAD + 1) * SLOTS_PER_EPOCH length after every process_proposer_lookahead execution?
checklist.test_procedure: 1. Verify the BeaconState definition declares proposer_lookahead as Vector[ValidatorIndex, (MIN_SEED_LOOKAHEAD + 1) * SLOTS_PER_EPOCH] in each client. 2. Verify the type is a fixed-length Vector, not a variable-length List. 3. If the client uses a dynamic array type (e.g., Go slices, Java ArrayList), verify explicit length checks after shift-and-fill. 4. Measure len(state.proposer_lookahead) before and after process_proposer_lookahead execution. 5. Verify they are equal and both equal to (MIN_SEED_LOOKAHEAD + 1) * SLOTS_PER_EPOCH. 6. Test edge cases: What happens if process_proposer_lookahead is called twice in succession (should not happen but verify no corruption)? 7. Verify SSZ serialization/deserialization preserves exact array length. 8. Check clients using dynamic array types: Go slice, Rust Vec, Java List -- verify no append-without-shift or shift-without-append code paths. 9. Verify that the fork transition (upgrade_to_fulu) initializes proposer_lookahead with the correct length.
executable_checks: Invariant test: assert len(state.proposer_lookahead) == (MIN_SEED_LOOKAHEAD + 1) * SLOTS_PER_EPOCH before and after every epoch transition
SSZ round-trip test: Serialize and deserialize BeaconState, verify proposer_lookahead length is preserved
Fork transition test: Verify upgrade_to_fulu produces proposer_lookahead of correct length
Crash test: If array length is wrong, verify get_beacon_proposer_index does not panic on out-of-bounds access
checklist.notes: Source: PROP-0044, Invariant: FULU-SG008-INV-003, Threat: stride-011, Trust Boundary: tb-009. Array length change would cause index-out-of-bounds crashes or incorrect proposer lookups. SSZ fixed-size Vector typing should prevent this at the serialization layer, but implementations using dynamic arrays (Go slices, Rust Vec) might not enforce this at runtime. A length mismatch would also cause SSZ merkleization to produce different state roots.

checklist.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity: Does the proposer lookahead contain valid proposer assignments for epoch N+1 at the start of epoch N, ensuring validators can prepare block proposals in advance?
checklist.test_procedure: 1. At the start of epoch N (first slot), read state.proposer_lookahead. 2. Extract entries for epoch N+1: positions [SLOTS_PER_EPOCH, 2*SLOTS_PER_EPOCH). 3. Verify all entries are valid validator indices (exist in the validator registry). 4. Verify all referenced validators are active in epoch N+1. 5. Verify the entries match what get_beacon_proposer_indices(state, N+1) would independently compute. 6. Test the fork transition: At the first epoch after upgrade_to_fulu, verify the lookahead contains valid assignments for the next epoch. 7. Verify that when epoch N+1 arrives and those entries are consumed via get_beacon_proposer_index, the proposers match what was pre-computed. 8. Check: At epoch 0 after fork activation, is the full lookahead correctly populated? 9. Verify the proposer_lookahead covers exactly MIN_SEED_LOOKAHEAD + 1 epochs worth of data, and that epoch N+1 data is always present.
executable_checks: End-to-end test: Run epoch transition, verify proposer_lookahead[SLOTS_PER_EPOCH:2*SLOTS_PER_EPOCH] contains valid indices for epoch N+1
Fork transition test: After upgrade_to_fulu, verify all lookahead entries reference active validators
Consistency test: For every slot in epoch N+1, verify get_beacon_proposer_index returns the same value that was in the lookahead at the start of epoch N
checklist.notes: Source: PROP-0045, Invariant: FULU-SG008-INV-004, Trust Boundary: tb-009. The deterministic proposer lookahead (EIP-7917) enables validators to prepare for their proposal duties in advance. Missing or invalid future-epoch proposer assignments would prevent validators from preparing blocks, increasing missed slot rate. Note: bug_bounty_eligible=false but still in-scope for audit. This is most likely to fail during the Fulu fork transition when the field is first populated.
